| 21 | Portal/recruiting implications tied to staff | The defining subject for this programme, and the guide treats it as a deliberate model under test. North Dakota State took a different approach from most, signing 29 high school players and only nine transfers, of whom three played at Power Four programmes last season — one being punter Caleb McGrath — while losing significant talent including two First-Team All-MVFC offensive linemen. The guide explains why the model worked before and why it may not now: recruiting and developing high school players succeeded at the FCS level, but Group of Five teams constantly retool with castoffs and former top prospects seeking a new home. With just 10 starters back and zero portal starters added, it leaves the question genuinely open. |
| 22 | VSiN author's assessment of coaching | A formula, not just a team, under examination. The guide identifies roster construction as the distinguishing factor — a largely homegrown roster and few transfers, with Tim Polasek having lost considerable talent to the portal — and frames the season as a true test of the programme's formula. Its reasoning is specific: portal losses were immense with little brought back, and while the Mountain West is no power conference, these are teams built with former Power Four players carrying real talent, so there should be doubts about walking in and dominating. Its summary is that the days of bullying a lesser conference are gone. |
| 23 | Coaching strengths | Full staff continuity, a quarterback who has been in the system since 2022, a programme record of five drafted starting quarterbacks in 11 years, and familiarity with the favorite's role — NDSU was favored in every game last season and closed as a 30-plus point favorite in six of 13. |
| 24 | Coaching concerns | A roster model the guide says is being tested for the first time at this level, immense portal losses including two First-Team All-MVFC offensive linemen with zero portal starters added, only 10 returning starters, the loss of the top two rushers and top two receivers, and a schedule with road trips to Air Force, UNLV, New Mexico and Hawaii the guide calls coin-flip spots. |

## VSiN Stability Score — as printed

Steve Makinen's Stability Score (pp. 41–44), reproduced exactly. This library does not recompute it, re-weight it, or substitute a TTW score.

| --- | --- | --- |
| Head coach returns | 4 | Returning head coach |

> The guide's own use of this number: it plays on teams with a Stability Score edge of 6 or more in non-conference games in weeks 0–3, and against teams scoring 0–6 in the same window, excluding games with a spread of 30 or more (pp. 40–41).
